title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.

findings.explanation: The diff does not introduce any raw SQL queries or string concatenation into SQL statements. The changes involve Django ORM filters (e.g., `self.backchannel_providers.filter`) and standard Django model operations, which are safe against SQL injection by default.

The `SSFStreamViewSet` is modified to include `DestroyModelMixin`, enabling the DELETE endpoint. However, the viewset inherits from `GenericViewSet` and does not explicitly define a `permission_classes` attribute. In the authentik framework (and standard Django REST Framework configurations for this project), the default permission classes typically enforce authentication and authorization checks (e.g., `IsAuthenticated` or specific policy-based permissions) globally or via the API router. The diff does not show any code that bypasses these checks or exposes the endpoint to unauthenticated users. The `queryset` is `Stream.objects.all()`, but without evidence of a missing permission class in the global settings or the viewset definition, we assume the standard framework protections are in place. No IDOR is evident as the viewset uses standard DRF routing which relies on the `pk` and standard permission checks.
